claims.claim: Need a Slack workspace as dev workspace
claims.quote: Select the Workspace where you'll be developing your app.

claims.quote: Your app has been installed on 10 or more active workspaces / An active workspace is a workspace that has been used in the past 28 days.

claims.quote: your landing page needs to be publicly accessible (i.e. not behind a login) / All Slack Marketplace apps must include a clear privacy policy

claims.claim: Create app via api.slack.com/apps?new_app=1 -> Create New App -> Blank app, choose dev workspace
claims.quote: Select Blank app. Click Continue. / Select the Workspace where you'll be developing your app.
claims.correction: Page's button is labeled 'Create an app', not 'Create New App'; 'Create New App' wording not found. Blank app and workspace selection confirmed. The new_app=1 URL itself is behind a button, not quoted.

claims.claim: Add scopes in OAuth & Permissions and HTTPS Redirect URL(s)
claims.quote: Alternatively, you can configure a Redirect URL in the App Management page under OAuth & Permissions.
claims.correction: S2 does not mention Redirect URL; cite S1 only for the redirect part. S2 confirms 'Within OAuth & Permissions, scroll down to Scopes.'

claims.claim: Install to Workspace, Allow; token under OAuth Tokens
claims.quote: Install your app by selecting the Install to Workspace button. ... Select Allow ... You'll see an access token under OAuth Tokens.

claims.claim: Authorize URL with client_id, scope/user_scope, state
claims.quote: To request scopes, redirect Slack users to `https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize`. / provide a `user_scope` parameter ... instead of, or in addition to, the `scope` parameter.
claims.correction: client_id and state-as-parameter wording not separately quoted (paraphrase only for client_id); state check is quoted under step-5.

claims.claim: Verify state, exchange code via oauth.v2.access, code expires in ten minutes
claims.quote: That's your temporary authorization code, which expires after ten minutes. / Check the `state` parameter if you sent one along with your initial user redirect.

claims.claim: Send same redirect_uri in both calls if several Redirect URLs configured
claims.quote: the parameter value must be the same for both steps — otherwise, you will encounter a `bad_redirect_uri` error
claims.correction: Note: the page's own text varies between `redirect_uri` and `redirect_url` for this sentence; the actual OAuth parameter is redirect_uri.

claims.claim: Manage Distribution -> checklist -> Activate Public Distribution
claims.quote: Scroll to Share Your App with Other Workspaces within the Manage Distribution section. ... Ensure all items in the supplied checklist are completed. ... Click Activate Public Distribution.

claims.claim: A collaborator on the app

claims.correction: Source is S5 only.

claims.correction: 'Extensive-data scopes not permitted' is too strong: page says broad message/file access is 'unlikely to be approved'. Legacy/restricted: 'DON'T request'.

claims.quote: the preliminary part of the review takes up to 10 business days to receive feedback / the functional review takes up to 10 weeks for new submissions / 6 weeks for published apps resubmitting changes / We are unable to skip or accelerate the review process in order to coordinate with your launch

claims.quote: As of February 19, 2020, your app must use TLS version 1.2 or greater to continue using Slack endpoints. / your app must use the state parameter when requesting access to customer data during the OAuth flow
claims.correction: Source is S5, not S4 (S4 has none of these). Signing secret/mTLS: only found 'The signing secret should be protected like a password' and 'These methods should be used instead of verification tokens'; exact 'signing secret or mTLS' requirement is paraphrase only.

claims.correction: No timing found, matching guide.

claims.quote: the functional review takes up to 10 weeks for new submissions

claims.quote: Your app has been installed on 10 or more active workspaces

claims.claim: ~1-3 h hands-on estimate
claims.correction: Author's own estimate; no official page states it.

claims.correction: agent_can_do says 'under 10 words'; official is '10 words (or fewer)'. Step 8 is correct.

claims.claim: Localhost redirect URLs not addressed
claims.quote: Desktop redirects (custom URI schemes and localhost) can't request bot scopes.
claims.correction: Localhost redirects are now mentioned, in the PKCE changelog (Mar 30 2026), in the context of PKCE-enabled apps and desktop redirects. Note: S1 itself still does not address localhost and states redirect_uri must use HTTPS; treat localhost as supported only for PKCE-enabled public-client apps, and verify before relying.

claims.claim: Max number of Redirect URLs unknown
claims.correction: Not stated on S1; still unknown.

claims.claim: Rate limits not on pages read
claims.correction: Not checked/not on pages fetched; remains unknown for these pages.

claims.claim: Token rotation applicability
claims.quote: Token rotation may not be turned off once it's turned on. / With token rotation, it expires every 12 hours.
claims.correction: Can now be resolved: rotation is opt-in (enabled by the app), irreversible, 12-hour access tokens; Marketplace apps 'can have' it enabled via Published App Settings (not stated as mandatory). PKCE-enabled apps: refresh tokens expire after 30 days; custom-URI-scheme installs always get rotating tokens (changelog).

claims.claim: Admin approval time unknown
claims.correction: No timing found on S3 (consistent).

missing: PKCE became GA on 2026-03-30: 'PKCE can now be enabled directly in your app settings without contacting Slack support.' Enabling is one-way, PKCE params are required for custom URI scheme redirects, refresh tokens expire after 30 days (changelog URL above).
Token rotation: once turned on it cannot be turned off; access tokens then expire every 12 hours (using-token-rotation page).

Marketplace requires TLS 1.2+ and use of the state parameter (S5), and the SSL requirement list for redirect/interaction/options-load/Events URLs (S3) - the guide attributes some of these to the wrong source.
